model: SeedVR2 (VAE encoder + windowed-attention DiT + VAE decoder, video SR/restoration)

notes: Per dev_roofline_profiling SKILL.md: preprocess.xml (bicubic_pillow Interpolate) upsamples the
864x496 source to the TARGET 1920x1088 canvas BEFORE the VAE encoder ever runs -- confirmed by
the real measured reference run (SeedVR2/orbix-seedvr2/mem_report_1080P_full_utf8.log) showing
the encoder's own conv_in input already at [1,3,T,1088,1920], and the VAE mid-block/DiT latent
grid at 136x240 == 1088/8 x 1920/8. So ALL THREE submodels (encoder, DiT, decoder) run at the
1920x1088-derived latent grid; the 864x496 input only sets the conditioning video's native res.
Shapes below are taken DIRECTLY from that real measured run (same target resolution, same txt=58,
f16 activations/weights throughout, no quantization) -- not re-derived/guessed from first
principles. Call counts are per-shape totals observed across the WHOLE encode/decode of the
121-frame video (i.e. already 'calls_per_inference' for that one submodel), taking the dominant
(most-frequent) shape class per logical layer and ignoring rare INIT/edge-segment variants
(<5 calls each) per SKILL.md's 'ignore tiny ops' guidance.
GroupNorm is NOT ov::op::v12::GroupNormalization -- the exported IR uses the SeedVR2-project-
specific ov::op::internal::GroupNormalizationZSplit (confirmed via grep on SeedVR2/ir/*.xml).
The VAE ENCODER's exported IR has ZERO CausalConv3DCarry nodes (grep type="CausalConv3DCarry"
SeedVR2/ir/vae_encoder_active.xml -> 0 matches, only 27 type="Convolution") -- causal temporal
history there is composed graph-side (carry_in Parameter -> Concat with body -> plain
Convolution -> Slice carry_out), so every encoder conv entry below uses kind=plain with t_body
already set to the POST-CONCAT total T extent (original per-segment body frames + (kt-stride_t)
carry frames), NOT the fused op. The VAE DECODER's IR, in contrast, has 33 CausalConv3DCarry
nodes (grep on vae_decoder_active.xml) and only 5 plain Convolution -- the decoder's 3x3x3 resnet
convs genuinely use the fused op, so decoder entries below keep kind=causal with t_body as the
per-segment body-only frame count (the op's own carry_in port supplies history separately).
1x1x1 shortcut/upscale convs and the kernel_t==1 spatial-only downsamplers are always plain
ov::op::v1::Convolution in both submodels (no temporal context needed).
DiT attention is windowed/variable-length (WindowQkvPrep + VarlenAttention in the reference log) --
maps directly onto the existing vlsdpa_bench (ov::op::internal::VLSDPA, CM kernel) family.
DiT FC/VAE-attention-FC weights are plain F16 (no INT4/INT8 compression) -- use fc_bench precision=f16.
CORRECTED (2026-10-15): the mem_report_1080P_full_utf8.log reference above was a SEPARATE (orbix)
reference implementation's memory log, not the real OpenVINO pipeline. Re-grounded against the REAL
OV_VERBOSE=4 execution trace of the actual IR files (SeedVR2/ir/seedvr2_verbose_1080P.log, 163MB,
1.69M lines, device='Intel(R) Arc(TM) B390 GPU'==PTL), which directly compiles/runs dit.xml,
preprocess.xml, vae_encoder_initializing/active.xml, vae_decoder_init/active.xml. Weight-constant
shapes (e.g. decoder.conv_in.weight layout f16:bfzyx:512x16x3x3x3, mid_block.resnets.0.conv1.weight
512x512x3x3x3) and activation shapes (SEEDVR2_DIT_BOUNDARY shape=[252960,2560] / [58,2560] lines)
confirm every channel/kernel/hidden_size/video_tokens/txt_tokens value below was ALREADY correct --
no shape changes needed.
ONE call-count correction was needed and KEPT: the VAE decoder uses K=4 tiles (a 2x2 spatial grid,
NOT 4 pure H-only tiles -- see the shape correction below) at this 1080p output resolution. Evidence:
'seedvr2_vae_decoder_init_fused_carry_op' and
'seedvr2_vae_decoder_active_fused_carry_op' are each independently compiled exactly 4 times (distinct
'Build model name' events), vs the VAE encoder's 'seedvr2_vae_encoder_init'/'_active' each compiled
exactly ONCE (no tiling there). Crucially, EACH of the decoder's 8 compiles independently contains
the FULL 33-node CausalConv3DCarry topology (264 total creates / 8 compiles = 33/compile, matching
vae_decoder_active.xml's own node count exactly) -- i.e. each tile-compile is a genuine independent
copy of the WHOLE decoder graph, not a fraction of it. So decoder conv/groupnorm/fc/attention calls
below are multiplied by 4 vs the previous (1 INIT + 29 ACTIVE = 30 segment-only) counts.
CORRECTED AGAIN (2026-10-15, same day): the x4 'calls' multiplier above was right, but the h/w SHAPES
were initially left at the FULL (untiled) frame size -- wrong, since real per-tile execution operates
on a SMALLER (core+halo) spatial extent per tile, not the full frame 4 times over. Found the exact
per-tile core+halo geometry directly from the verbose log's non-constant 'calc_output_layouts'/
parameter layout lines for every '*.carry_in' Parameter (these reveal REAL per-tile activation
shapes, not just weight-constant shapes): e.g. 'parameter:decoder.mid_block.resnets.0.conv1.carry_in
output tensor: f16:bfzyx:1x512x2x72x122:nopad' and 'parameter:decoder.conv_out.carry_in output
tensor: f16:bfzyx:1x128x2x576x976:nopad'. This proves the real tiling is a 2x2 GRID (halved H AND
halved W per tile, not a pure 1D H-split): base latent tier (full 136x240) tiles to 72x122 (core
68x120 + halo_h=4/halo_w=2), and halo scales by the SAME factor as the tier's own upsample ratio at
each subsequent tier (confirmed directly for all 4 tiers via up_blocks.{0,1,2}.upsamplers.0.conv.carry_in
and decoder.conv_out.carry_in): tier1 (272x480 full) -> 144x244 tile (halo_h=8/halo_w=4); tier2
(544x960 full) -> 288x488 tile (halo_h=16/halo_w=8); tier3/pixel-res (1088x1920 full) -> 576x976 tile
(halo_h=32/halo_w=16, exactly matching decoder.conv_out.carry_in's directly-observed 576x976). All
vae_decoder conv/groupnorm/fc/attention h/w (and fc 'm'/attention 's', which are h*w-derived) below
are now these REAL per-tile values, not the full-frame values -- this requires fresh conv_bench/
groupnorm_bench/sdpa_bench runs at the new (smaller) shapes on remote PTL (the 'calls'=4x-per-tile
multiplier itself needed no re-run, since it's a pure report-time multiplier, but the SHAPE change
does need new measurements -- a per-op kernel's time/efficiency is shape-dependent, cannot be inferred
from the old full-frame measurement). Groupnorm entry names renamed to match their new tile h/w
(e.g. gn_c512_h136w240 -> gn_c512_h72w122) since the name previously encoded the (now wrong) shape.
A SECOND apparent correction was investigated and REJECTED after cross-validation: the log also
shows 33 distinct DiT model compiles ('stage0'..'stage32', plus matching SEEDVR2_DIT_GPU/
SEEDVR2_DIT_STAGE index=0..32 instrumentation). This superficially looks like '33 diffusion steps',
but TWO pieces of evidence prove it is instead 33 memory-managed PER-LAYER pipeline stages of a
SINGLE forward pass (compile one layer's weights, infer, release, move to the next): (a) VLSDPA op
creates total only 32 across the WHOLE log (== num_layers, i.e. ONE VLSDPA node per stage on
average) -- if each stage recompiled the FULL 32-layer model, VLSDPA creates would be 32*33=1056,
not 32; (b) each stage's own compile_ms is only ~3.5s (range 2.1-7.7s) -- far too short to compile a
full 32-layer, hidden_size=2560 transformer stack from scratch, but exactly consistent with
compiling ONE layer's worth of ops. A compute-bound roofline sanity check confirms this: at M=
252960 tokens, JUST the vid_qkv FC alone needs >=169ms/call at 100% of this platform's 58.982
FP16 TFLOPS peak, so 33x1 all-layer recompiles (33*32=1056 vid_qkv calls) would need >=178s for
vid_qkv ALONE at perfect efficiency -- already exceeding the real measured TOTAL DiT infer_ms across
all 33 stages (85,086 ms = 85.09s, SEEDVR2_DIT_STAGE infer_ms summed). So DiT calls below are kept
UNCHANGED at their original single-forward-pass counts (32/31/1 per layer-type, 16/16 for the two
alternating window-attention configs) -- NOT multiplied by 33.
External validation of the (now corrected) totals against this real production run's own measured
wall-clock, as a sanity check (not an exact-match expectation, since isolated single-op microbenches
vs a fused/pipelined whole-model compiled graph can legitimately differ): this file's roofline-
projected DiT total (kernel-time x calls, unchanged calls) is ~53.4s vs the real run's measured
85,086 ms (85.09s) DiT infer_ms -- a 62.8% ratio. The roofline-projected decoder total (kernel-time
x 4x-corrected calls) is ~276.99s*... see outputs/seedvr2/SUMMARY for the exact post-correction
figure vs the real run's 'vae_decoder' module run=402,113.3 ms (402.11s, includes compile+infer for
all 8 compiles) -- both ratios land in a similar, plausible 60-70% range, consistent with expected
bench-isolation-vs-real-fused-execution overhead in either direction, not a methodology red flag.
LESSON for future re-groundings: 'N distinct ProgramBuilder compiles for logically-the-same-named
model' does NOT by itself mean 'multiply calls by N' -- always cross-check whether each compile
contains the FULL op topology (-> genuine N-fold replication, e.g. decoder's H-tiles) or only a
FRACTION of it (-> memory-managed staging of ONE pass, e.g. DiT's per-layer stages), via a node-type
total-count-vs-per-compile-count comparison plus a compute-bound sanity check against any available
real measured wall-clock timing.
